blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Home Extension Cost in Southbank in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking of extending your Southbank home? We break down typical costs per square metre, council fees, and factors that affect your budget in inner-Melbourne.
body: Adding a home extension in Southbank is a popular way to gain more space without moving. But costs can vary dramatically depending on site access, existing structure, and your choice of finishes. In 2026, average build costs for a single-storey extension in inner Melbourne range from $3,500 to $6,000 per square metre. For a typical 30sqm living area, that's $105,000 to $180,000 — excluding design and council fees.

Your site's unique conditions matter a lot. Southbank properties often sit on narrow lots with challenging access for machinery. If your extension requires underpinning or structural changes to the existing building, add 10-20% to your budget. Also check your heritage overlay status — many areas in Southbank have strict design guidelines that can add $5,000-$15,000 in consultant and compliance costs.

Council fees in Melbourne City Council (which covers Southbank) typically include a building permit ($2,000-$4,000), a planning permit if needed ($1,500-$5,000), and a public liability bond. Don't forget GST — at 10% it bumps every line item. A realistic total for a mid-range extension is $130,000 to $220,000. Quality fixtures and finishes push that higher.

The timing of your build also affects cost. Summer demand drives up tradie rates. Winter can slow concrete and roofing work. We recommend starting design in autumn so you're ready for a spring build. Henny's fixed-price approach means you lock in costs before a single shovel hits the ground — no surprises when material prices rise.

One tip: engage your builder early. With early contractor involvement, we can value-engineer your design to stay within budget. For example, choosing a flat roof instead of pitched can save $10,000-$15,000. Repositioning windows to avoid structural walls also cuts costs. We've helped Southbank homeowners save up to 20% on their extension budget this way.

Finally, think about return on investment. A well-designed extension in Southbank can add 15-25% to your property value. With median house prices over $1.5 million in the area, that's a significant upside. Don't cut corners on quality — invest in good design and proper council approvals. Henny's after-care program means your extension is guaranteed for 12 months. For a personalised quote, get in touch.

blogPosts.title: Design & Construct vs Construction Management: Which Is Best for Your Fitzroy Project?
blogPosts.excerpt: Understanding the difference between D&C and construction management is crucial for your Fitzroy build. We compare both approaches to help you pick the right one.
body: If you're planning a building project in Fitzroy, one of the first decisions is how to structure your contract. Two popular options are Design & Construct (D&C) and Construction Management (CM). Each suits different project types, budgets, and risk appetites. We'll walk you through both so you can make an informed choice.

D&C means one company — like Henny — handles both the design and the construction. You get a single point of contact, a fixed price, and a guaranteed timeline. This works well for residential extensions or small commercial fit-outs where the scope is clear. The downside: less flexibility to change your mind mid-project without cost variations.

Construction Management, on the other hand, keeps you in control. Henny acts as your agent, procuring separate trades and managing the schedule. You pay for actual costs plus a management fee. This is ideal for complex projects like multi-storey developments or heritage renovations in Fitzroy, where you want to choose your own architects and subcontractors.

Cost is a major factor. With D&C, you know the price upfront — typically a lump sum. With CM, the final cost is only known when the project ends, though we give detailed estimates. For a typical Fitzroy townhouse renovation, D&C might be $400,000 fixed, while CM could range from $380,000 to $450,000 depending on site discoveries.

Risk allocation differs too. In D&C, Henny bears most of the risk — if a steel price spikes, we absorb it. In CM, the owner takes the risk. That's why CM is often chosen by experienced developers who want transparency. For first-timers, D&C offers peace of mind. We always discuss both at our initial consultation.

At Henny, we've delivered projects under both models across Fitzroy, Glen Iris, and Southbank. Our advice: if your project has a clear brief and you want a fixed price, go D&C. If you're working with a heritage overlay or want to cherry-pick specialists, CM gives you flexibility. Either way, we'll guide you through the process. Contact us to chat about your Fitzroy project.

blogPosts.title: The Complete Guide to Social Housing Construction in Melbourne's Inner Suburbs
blogPosts.excerpt: Social housing projects require specialist knowledge of funding, compliance, and community engagement. We share insights from our Lincoln Square project in Southbank.
body: Social housing is a growing priority for the Victorian Government, with targets to build thousands of new homes across Melbourne. For builders, these projects offer long-term stability but come with unique challenges. At Henny, we delivered Lincoln Square in Southbank — a 28-unit social housing development — and learned plenty along the way.

Funding is the first hurdle. Most social housing projects rely on government grants, NHFIC loans, or partnerships with community housing providers. You'll need to demonstrate cost certainty and a track record. Our fixed-price D&C approach gave confidence to funders at Lincoln Square. We also had to adhere to strict sustainability standards, including 7-star NatHERS energy ratings.

Compliance is another layer. Social housing must meet the Design Guidelines for Social Housing (DGSH) published by the Department of Families, Fairness and Housing. These cover everything from minimum apartment sizes to accessibility and communal spaces. For example, all units at Lincoln Square have a minimum 10sqm of private open space. We worked closely with council to ensure every detail was signed off.

Community engagement is critical. Residents in existing social housing estates can be anxious about redevelopment. We held open days, provided regular updates, and ensured minimal disruption during construction. For Lincoln Square, we even employed local subcontractors from Southbank and nearby suburbs, boosting the local economy.

Timelines can be tight but are often fixed by funding agreements. Our project management team kept Lincoln Square on schedule despite supply chain delays. We pre-ordered key materials like windows and joinery months in advance. On-site safety is paramount — social housing sites often have vulnerable neighbours, so we maintained strict zoning and noise controls.

If you're a community housing provider or developer considering a social housing project, reach out to Henny. We have experience with NHFIC compliance, DGSH standards, and delivering on time. Social housing is more than a building — it's a community asset. Let's build one together.

blogPosts.title: Building in Melbourne's Climate: Tips for Structural Weatherproofing in Southbank
blogPosts.excerpt: Melbourne's four-seasons-in-one-day weather demands robust building techniques. Here's how we weatherproof our projects in Southbank and beyond.
body: Melbourne's climate is famously unpredictable — hot northerly winds one day, cold southerly change the next. For builders in Southbank, this means designing structures that can handle thermal expansion, wind loads, and heavy rain. At Henny, we integrate weatherproofing from day one on every project.

Roofing is the front line. We use Colorbond steel with concealed fixings on flat roofs to reduce leaks. For pitched roofs, we specify a breathable membrane under the tiles to prevent condensation. Trusted brands like Lysaght and Bluescope are our go-to. In the 2025 Lincoln Square project, we installed a green roof on part of the building — it not only insulates but also manages stormwater runoff.

Windows and doors are vulnerable points. We choose thermally broken aluminium frames with double glazing — preferably from Australian manufacturers like Capral. The frames include drainage channels and weather seals that meet AS 2047 for wind resistance. In high-exposure Southbank areas, we specify wind-rated doors that can handle gusts over 200km/h.

Waterproofing is non-negotiable. We apply two coats of liquid membrane to wet areas, with a minimum 2mm thickness. For balconies, we use a polyurethane system with a protective screed. All joins are taped and sealed. We also install cavity drainage systems behind cladding to prevent moisture trapping. This is critical in Melbourne where humidity spikes in summer.

Concrete work needs special care. In winter, we add accelerators to prevent frost damage during curing. In summer, we keep slabs wet and shaded to avoid crazing. Expansion joints are placed every 6-8 metres. For exposed aggregate driveways, we seal them annually to protect against UV degradation. Our concrete suppliers verify each batch meets AS 1379.

The best advice: over-specify now, save money later. Investing $5,000 extra in waterproofing can prevent $50,000 in water damage down the track. At Henny, every project includes a detailed weatherproofing plan, reviewed at each stage. We also offer maintenance programs to check seals and membranes annually. Contact us to discuss your Southbank build — let's make it weather-ready.
